S11.01.note: The code gives aria-labels on these buttons; the spoken result itself is not verified by reading code.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar to open the sidebar.
Turn on VoiceOver and move across the header buttons 'Sessions', 'Settings', 'New chat' and 'More actions'.
Check that each one is announced by its name and what it does, as in Expected.
S11.01.where: AGI Code icon in the VS Code Activity Bar > sidebar header buttons 'Sessions', 'Settings', 'New chat', 'More actions'

S11.02.note: Which Settings nav section holds 'Model and reasoning' was not confirmed.
steps: Click the 'Settings' button in the AGI Code sidebar header.
Turn on VoiceOver and use its heading navigation to jump between headings.
Check the top heading is 'Settings' and sections such as 'Model and reasoning' are headings below it.
S11.02.where: Settings (gear button) > page titled 'Settings' with section headings such as 'Model and reasoning'. The empty chat also has the heading 'Start a conversation'.

S11.03.note: The menu keyboard handler (wireMenuKeyboard) handles Escape and Tab; the Arrow key branch was counted, not fully read.
steps: Press Tab until the 'More actions' button has focus, then press Enter.
Press the Down Arrow key to move between the menu items.
Press Escape to close the menu and check the menu closes with no mouse.
S11.03.where: 'More actions' button (the ellipsis icon) in the AGI Code sidebar > menu items 'Output style', 'Next message effort', 'Focus view'

steps: Click in the 'Chat input' box, then press Tab repeatedly.
Look at each focused button for a visible outline ring.
Check the focused control is always clearly outlined, as in Expected.
S11.04.where: Tab key on any control in the AGI Code sidebar; the focus outline is a style rule (button:focus-visible)

S11.05.note: The Escape-to-close handling was not read; only the Tab trap code was read.
steps: Open the Command Palette and type 'Show Getting Started', then press Enter.
Press Tab repeatedly and check focus stays inside the dialog (Next and links).
Press Escape and check the dialog closes, as in Expected.
S11.05.where: Command Palette > 'Code: Show Getting Started' opens the dialog 'Work with your code' (role dialog)

steps: Press Tab until 'More actions' has focus, then press Enter to open the menu.
Press Escape to close the menu.
Check focus is back on the 'More actions' button, as in Expected.
S11.06.where: 'More actions' button > menu, then Escape in the AGI Code sidebar

S11.07.needs: a signed-in account that can get a reply
S11.07.note: The code line cited for this item (webviewContent.ts:3122) is the developer runtime status region, not a reply-finished announcement; the completion announcement itself was not located.
steps: Turn on VoiceOver, click 'Chat input', type a short message and send it with Enter.
Keep focus in the chat input while the reply runs.
Listen for a short announcement when the reply finishes, and check focus did not move, as in Expected.
S11.07.where: Inner behaviour: the sidebar's status regions (role 'status', aria-live 'polite') announce finished events while focus stays put

S11.08.needs: a signed-in account with a live provider reply (live-web)
S11.08.note: Code status unverified: the cited line no longer holds the quoted code. The transcript log region is aria-live polite with additions, which may announce every streamed chunk; not verified.
steps: Turn on VoiceOver and send a message that gets a long streamed reply.
Listen while the reply streams and count how often it is announced.
Check it is spoken calmly in chunks or once when done, not word by word, as in Expected.
S11.08.where: Inner behaviour: the transcript region (role 'log', aria-live 'polite', aria-relevant 'additions') announces a streaming reply

S11.09.needs: a signed-in account and a workspace folder open
S11.09.note: Which buttons show depends on the request type; the exact tool step states were read from tool-status.ts.
steps: Make sure a workspace folder is open and send a request that asks AGI to change a file or run a command.
When the card 'Approval needed' appears, turn on VoiceOver and move through it.
Check the card announces its summary and state, and that the approve and deny buttons have names, as in Expected.
S11.09.where: Chat > send a request that needs approval (for example a file edit or shell command) > card titled 'Approval needed' with status and approve or deny buttons

S11.11.needs: a workspace with a text file
S11.11.note: Drop onto the composer is the drag path (webviewContent.ts around line 7720). No resize or reorder control was found in the code.
steps: Click the '+' button labelled 'Attach or use tools' next to the chat input.
Click 'Attach workspace files' and pick a text file, instead of dragging.
Check the file is attached without any drag, as in Expected.
S11.11.where: '+' button ('Attach or use tools') in the composer > 'Attach workspace files'

S11.14.needs: a Mac with Reduce motion on and a reply in progress
S11.14.note: The rule is a CSS media query for prefers-reduced-motion in webviewContent.ts; the app has no own setting for it.
steps: Turn on the Mac's Reduce motion setting.
Open AGI Code, send a message and watch the spinning icon while the reply is pending.
Check the spinner stops or is replaced, as in Expected.
S11.14.where: Inner behaviour: the sidebar's looping spinner icons (for example a pending reply or a running tool step) are turned off by the Mac's reduced-motion setting

S11.21.needs: a Japanese, Chinese or Korean input method on the Mac
S11.21.note: The guard is in the keydown handler that returns early when isComposing is true.
steps: Switch the Mac to a Japanese input method (or Chinese or Korean).
Click 'Chat input' and type a word so the text is still being composed.
Press Enter to confirm the conversion and check the message is NOT sent, the text stays in the box.
S11.21.where: 'Chat input' box in the AGI Code composer

S11.22.needs: a paid account with a usage meter (Free shows no meters)
S11.22.note: The label is written as 'Usage & billing' in the file. Dates use the browser locale. Token counts in webviewContent.ts (around line 5687) are hard-coded to en-US. Chat language follows vscode.env.language (l10n/index.ts).
steps: Change VS Code's display language to another language and restart VS Code.
Open Settings from the AGI Code sidebar and click 'Usage & billing'.
Compare the reset date and numbers with your system format, as in Expected.
S11.22.where: Settings > 'Usage & billing' (plan usage line such as '% used · resets <date>')

S11.24.needs: a signed-in account and a prompt that runs tools
S11.24.note: The exact visible spot of the activity count was not confirmed; plural forms come from Intl.PluralRules.
steps: Change VS Code's display language to Spanish or French and restart VS Code.
Send a request that makes AGI run several tool steps.
Read the count, and compare one step ('1 acción') with several ('3 acciones'), as in Expected.
S11.24.where: A chat reply that runs several tool steps shows a count such as '3 actions' (the activity summary)

S11.25.needs: a way to make a reply fail
S11.25.note: The error key chatError.generic is shown for unknown failures. Forcing a failure on demand was not confirmed.
steps: Change VS Code's display language to Spanish or French and restart VS Code.
Cause a failed reply (for example a provider timeout or an invalid request).
Read the error text and check it is in that language, as in Expected.
S11.25.where: Chat > a failed reply shows the error text in the reply area, with a 'Retry' button

S11.26.note: The code writes the word 'Cmd' (not the symbol ⌘) on Mac (webviewContent.ts line 4458). The visible spot of the hint text was not fully confirmed.
steps: Open Settings and set 'Send key' to the modifier option.
Go back to the chat and check the send hint or tooltip.
Compare the modifier text with Expected: it should show Cmd on Mac and Ctrl elsewhere.
S11.26.where: Settings > 'Send key' (composer.enterBehavior), then the 'Send' button in the composer (tooltip 'Send (Enter)')

S11.27.needs: a narrow sidebar and another display language
S11.27.note: The plan gives no code location. CSS overflow and ellipsis rules exist in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts, but per-control behaviour was not verified.
steps: Change VS Code's display language to German and restart VS Code.
Narrow the AGI Code sidebar and open Settings > 'Usage & billing'.
Check long labels wrap or truncate without overlapping or clipping controls, as in Expected.
S11.27.where: Inner layout rule: long labels in the AGI Code sidebar and Settings at a narrow width
